definition.simple: When two indicators tend to say the same thing because they are calculated from the same prices.
definition.balanced: RSI, MACD and moving averages all use recent closing prices, so they often turn together. Their agreement is closer to one reading than to two confirmations. Information from a different source, such as structure or volume, is less likely to repeat it.

example: RSI 14 crosses above 50 and MACD crosses above zero on the same candle: largely the same message twice.
